stem.en: Kabir releases a marble from 40 cm up. It races down and climbs the far slope. Where does it stop, with no rubbing?

text.en: At 40 cm. Every bit of the potential energy it started with has turned back into potential energy.
Higher than 40 cm, because it picked up speed on the way.

feedback.en: Speed is what the fall bought. Climbing spends it. There is exactly enough to buy back 40 cm and not a centimetre more.

text.en: Lower than 40 cm, because going up is harder than going down.

feedback.en: With nothing rubbing, going up costs exactly what going down gave. The marble reaches 40 cm. Real rubbing makes it fall short, and that is the next slide.

text.en: At the bottom, because it is heavy.

feedback.en: Weight decides how hard the Earth pulls, but the height is the same for a light marble and a heavy one.

explanation.en: Potential energy at the start sets a budget. Kinetic energy is what the budget buys on the way down. It is all spent buying height back on the far side.
